newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican guerrillas say jailed man not their leader.
newsitem.headline: Mexican guerrillas say jailed man not their leader.

text.p: A Mexican guerrilla group on Wednesday denied that peasant rights activist Benigno Guzman, who was jailed earlier this week, was their leader.
The Popular Revolutionary Army (EPR) said Guzman and two others arrested did not belong to the armed Marxist group.
"To say these social fighters were leaders of the EPR is deceitful and grotesque," an EPR statement said.
The Interior Ministry announced on Monday that it had captured the EPR's "ringleader" at his home in Mexico City.
Authorities said the arrest as a breakthrough in their war against the EPR, a rebel group that sprung up in June last year saying it was fighting to overthrow the government.
EPR guerrillas have mainly attacked army and police posts, killing more than 30 people.
Guzman told Reuters in an interview from jail on Tuesday that the government was persecuting him by trying to link his peasant rights group to the guerrillas.
